title: Why Is Helport AI Limited (HPAI) Stock Down -8.33% Today?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* Helport AI shares fell 8.33% to $0.22 in Tuesday morning trade, extending a two-session slide that began with a 12.3% drop on Monday.
* The primary catalyst was the fiscal 2026 results release published after Monday's close: revenue fell 36.7% to $22.05 million, the company swung to a $26.15 million net loss, and management flagged substantial doubt about going-concern status.
* Secondary pressures included a $10.69 million noncash impairment, research and development spending rising to $18.85 million from $6.32 million, just $0.39 million of cash at June 30, 2026, and no quantitative fiscal 2027 guidance.
* The offsetting detail: AI+BPO services revenue jumped 575.9% to $1.44 million and category gross margin improved to 46.8%, though the business is still far too small to replace lost legacy revenue.
* Software shares were broadly softer, with the iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF ([IGV](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IGV/)) down about 2.1%, but the bulk of the decline was company-specific for this roughly $9 million market-cap micro-cap.
* **News Significance Score: 36/100** \- Material but partly pre-signaled results met a move only modestly larger than this stock's normal swing.
* Traders are now watching financing terms and dilution risk, any Nasdaq bid-price compliance update ahead of the mid-January 2027 deadline, and evidence that AI Labor deployments convert into reported revenue.

# Opening Summary

Helport AI Limited ([HPAI](https://tickeron.com/ticker/HPAI/)) is a Singapore-based artificial intelligence company that sells AI-assisted customer communication software and AI-enabled business process outsourcing to contact centers, mainly across Southeast Asia, with China-based clients having historically dominated its revenue. In Tuesday's session the stock traded at $0.22, down 8.33% from the prior close of $0.24, marking a second straight double-digit-percentage decline for the week. The move lower followed the company's fiscal 2026 results, released after Monday's closing bell, which showed a sharp revenue contraction, a large net loss, a nine-figure write-down in the millions, and a management warning about the company's ability to continue as a going concern. No analyst rating change or takeover development was involved; the driver was squarely the annual financial disclosure.

# Fiscal 2026 Results: A Loss, a Write-Down and a Going-Concern Warning

For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, Helport AI reported revenue of $22.05 million, down 36.7% from $34.86 million a year earlier. AI services revenue, the core software line, fell 40.5% to $20.61 million. The bottom line flipped from net income of $1.86 million to a net loss of $26.15 million, equal to a basic and diluted loss of $0.69 per share versus earnings of $0.05 a year ago.

The loss included a $10.69 million noncash impairment tied to software built for seven China-based customers, while research and development spending climbed to $18.85 million from $6.32 million as the company redirected resources toward autonomous "AI Labor" products. Most concerning for investors, cash stood at just $0.39 million at fiscal year-end against a working capital deficit of $13.28 million, and management explicitly flagged doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern and the need to raise additional capital. For a company valued at roughly $9 million, that combination of a shrinking top line, a going-concern disclosure and prospective equity issuance is the core of the bear case.

# China Exit Removes Roughly 93% of the Revenue Base

The revenue collapse was deliberate rather than purely cyclical. China-based customers accounted for approximately 93% of fiscal 2026 revenue. Beginning in January 2026, management reassessed regional profitability, extended payment cycles, collection risk and heavy customization demands on certain legacy engagements, then chose to gradually discontinue those relationships. Revenue from legacy China-focused AI services was nil from July 1, 2026 through November 16, 2026, and the company gave no quantitative fiscal 2027 guidance, leaving investors without a visible replacement revenue base.

# AI+BPO Growth: A Small Bright Spot That Cannot Yet Offset the Decline

The one clearly positive line item was AI+BPO services, where revenue rose 575.9% to $1.44 million and category gross margin improved to 46.8% from 11.8%, helped by heavier use of AI tooling and tighter computing-resource management. The company also disclosed that a Southeast Asian fintech engagement has generated average monthly revenue of roughly $200,000, and it is targeting a shift toward more autonomous AI execution in debt-collection workflows. Those are constructive data points, but they are far too small to absorb the loss of a business that produced more than $34 million a year ago, which is why the shares reacted to the headline numbers rather than the growth story.

# Market Context and Trading Activity

Activity was thin even by this stock's standards: roughly 15,000 shares changed hands in the first half hour of trading, against 157,900 shares on Monday and a three-month average near 3.55 million, a gap explained partly by the early-session timing and partly by the extremely limited float of about 8.1 million shares. The session's low of $0.21 took the stock beneath its previous 52-week low of $0.2313 and well below its 50-day moving average near $0.30 and 200-day average above $1.10. The broader tape added modest pressure - the software ETF ([IGV](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IGV/)) slipped about 2.1% and the Nasdaq-100 proxy ([QQQ](https://tickeron.com/ticker/QQQ/)) was roughly flat - but a company-specific filing of this magnitude, in a name already down more than 90% over 52 weeks, explains the direction far better than sector drift.

# News Significance Score

The score runs from 0, meaning no meaningful news and a move that is normal for the stock, to 100, meaning transformative news and an extreme, rare price move. Helport AI earns 36 out of 100. The verified news was genuinely material for a company this small: a 36.7% revenue decline, a swing to a $26.15 million loss, a $10.69 million impairment and an explicit going-concern warning, though part of the damage had been pre-signaled in the November 3 late-filing notice. The price reaction, by contrast, was unremarkable: today's 8.33% decline is about 1.85 times the stock's typical daily move of roughly 4.5%, and moves of 8% or more occurred eight times in the last 60 sessions. Strong news, ordinary volatility, hence a mid-range score.

# What Comes Next for HPAI

Attention now shifts to the formal annual report filing and to how management funds the business: any equity raise or convertible financing would resolve near-term liquidity questions but would dilute an already tiny share count. Nasdaq's minimum bid price notice, disclosed in July 2026 with a compliance window running toward mid-January 2027, keeps listing risk in view without a reverse split or a sustained recovery above $1. Investors will also look for the first fiscal 2027 interim report to see whether AI Labor and international deployments produce revenue that can replace the China book, and whether gross margins hold as the model shifts toward outcome-based pricing. The main risks are continued cash burn, slower-than-expected international ramp, further impairments, and the wide bid-ask spreads typical of thinly traded micro-caps.
